description:
Properly-scoped design follow-up to fz-go4.18.20's diagnose-only pass (2026-07-02, re-measured at e55c8e185). AnalyzeActivation(main) fires 22x on 00001 (12 distinct, 10 byte-identical no-change re-runs); callsite.defined fires 133x across 26 keys with 76 identical re-publications -- unchanged since the original fz-go4.18.12 measurement, confirmed NOT resolved by fz-go4.18.22's RuntimeDemand SCC-settle or the subsequent census/keystone arc.

ROOT CAUSE (proven, not suspected): suppression of spurious downstream wake is ALREADY correct -- a byte-identical re-analysis does not bump its output revision, so it does not itself cascade. The churn is a CROSS-ROUND batching gap: a caller's dependency on N callees means N separate single-fact revision bumps across N sequential ascent rounds, each independently re-enqueuing the caller's full AnalyzeActivation, because nothing yet detects "this dependency cone has settled -- stop re-running dependents until the whole cone concludes." The scheduler's existing coalesce (scheduler.rs coalesced_seen/enqueue_step) only merges simultaneous wakes WITHIN one applied step; it cannot merge wakes that arrive on different rounds.

DIRECTION (two candidate shapes, pick after investigation):
(a) SCC/round-settledness-gated re-analysis, mirroring fz-go4.18.22's proven bottom-start monotone-ascent-then-publish-once pattern for RuntimeDemand: hold a caller's re-analysis until its whole callee-dependency SCC/cone has settled for the current epoch, then run once. This is the more architecturally consistent choice given .18.22 already proved this shape works for a structurally similar problem (many members settling across rounds, one settle-then-publish instead of N republish-per-round).
(b) Granularize analyze_activation so a single callee revision only recomputes the ONE affected call site's contribution (a targeted re-derive), not a full re-walk of the caller's body -- avoids the whole-caller cost regardless of how many rounds the callee cone takes to settle.

SEQUENCING: this touches the same enqueue/wake paths (jobs/semantic.rs, scheduler.rs, world.rs revision/changed-wake machinery) that fz-go4.18.24's follow_up-to-pull migration is actively converting family-by-family. Do NOT start this concurrently with an in-flight fz-go4.18.24 family touching the same files -- sequence after, or coordinate explicitly if truly parallel work is needed.

RIDE-ALONG (cheap, separable, can land standalone first): return_type.defined telemetry lacks a `changed: bool` field that callsite.defined already has (root_id/function_id/ascents/rebased only) -- add it so the "45 fires / 8 changed" split fz-go4.18.20 originally reported can be independently re-verified without a noisy Ty-id-churn proxy.

ACCEPTANCE: identical callsite/return_type re-publications ~0 on the 00001/00181 corpus; AnalyzeActivation fire counts on 00001 justified by distinct input revisions (expect close to 12, not 22); suite green 3x, clippy/fmt clean; minimal-job-trace gate satisfied (job counts drop, products byte-identical).
title: SCC/round-settledness-gated re-analysis: collapse cross-round AnalyzeActivation churn
